channel.title: HSJ - Latest news
channel.description: Custom RSS feed for HSJ latest news

item.title: Chair takes on neighbouring trust
item.description: An acute trust is to share its chair with a neighbouring mental health and community trust, citing the “synergy” between the two.

item.title: NHSE abolition group chair hasn’t attended meetings for a year
item.description: Alan Milburn has not attended a meeting in his capacity as joint chair of the committee overseeing the abolition of NHS England for more than a year, HSJ can reveal.

item.title: Surgeon harm review delayed to 2027
item.description: A trust has apologised for a further delay to an independent review into potential harm to hundreds of patients, many of them children, treated by one of its surgeons.

item.title: Regional role for long-serving CEO
item.description: A long-serving trust chief will work part-time as director of a different NHS England region in an interim capacity.

item.title: CEO raises alarm over terror attack readiness
item.description: A chief executive who has led ambulance trusts for 23 years has warned that the sector is not “sufficiently trained, equipped, or resourced” to respond to a terrorist attack.

item.title: Consultants to strike next month
item.description: Medical consultants in England have announced two days of strikes next month over pay, conditions and workload.

item.title: Top CEOs fear politicians with ‘a different ideology’
item.description: The imminent re-establishment of direct political control over the NHS could see it diverted from delivering “what’s right for the population as a whole”, leading trust CEOs have warned.

item.title: Leaders lukewarm about key provider reforms
item.description: Leading trust chief executives are split on the desirability of becoming advanced foundation trusts, an HSJ roundtable has heard.

item.title: Inquiry trust appoints ex-nurse as substantive CEO
item.description: A trust undergoing an independent inquiry into its maternity and neonatal services has appointed its interim chief executive to the role permanently.

item.title: Cancer board dominated by national officials
item.description: Nearly two-thirds of the members of the reformed “independent” national cancer board are NHS England or Department of Health and Social Care officials, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Bed pressures now ‘relentless’, reports CQC
item.description: Mental health trusts are under “daily relentless pressure” on their inpatient beds, the Care Quality Commission has warned.

item.title: ICB expects one in 10 beds to close
item.description: England’s largest integrated care board expects to need almost a tenth fewer hospital beds within a decade as it tries to close a projected financial gap that could reach £4bn.

item.title: Surge in complaints about children’s care and refusal to refer
item.description: Complaints about paediatric care and GPs refusing to make referrals to specialist services leapt over the past year, HSJ analysis suggests, as overall concerns hit record levels.

item.title: No one cares about the NHS anymore… and that’s OK
item.description: Kemi Badenoch recently addressed a private meeting attended by senior parliamentarians. She was asked what the Conservatives’ health policy was and replied, ‘not to have one’

item.title: Exclusive: Ministers drop plan to scrap investigations body
item.description: The government has U-turned on its plan to abolish an independent health service investigations body after opposition in the House of Lords, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Chair quits after CQC finds ‘misaligned’ board
item.description: The chair of an embattled trust has announced he will step down amid warnings from the Care Quality Commission, HSJ has learned.

item.title: Cash ‘critical’ as 13,500 invoices go unpaid
item.description: An acute trust’s cash position is “critical”, with more than 13,500 invoices outstanding, its board has been warned.

item.title: Revealed: 10 child deaths investigated at trust facing prosecution
item.description: An independent review into 10 child fatalities has identified fundamental governance and sepsis care failings at an embattled trust, HSJ has discovered.

item.title: ICB exec pay under review after mergers
item.description: The government is considering steps to stop integrated care board executives receiving pay rises simply because their organisations merge and cover bigger populations.

item.title: Leaders ‘disconnected’ from front line at high-secure hospital
item.description: Bosses at a trust being investigated for corporate manslaughter have been criticised by a regulator, which found care and patient dignity failings, and a “disconnect” between senior leaders and frontline staff at its high-secure hospital.
